entries.title: Complex-description boundary in end-to-end 3D world construction
entries.frozen_irreducible_object: A measurable failure-regime boundary in end-to-end multimodal world construction: after RL raises overall executable 3D construction performance, long underspecified Complex Description and Scene Restatement queries remain below 50% Pass@1. The scientific object is not query difficulty in general, but the transition between queries that can be solved by the trained intent-layout-tool-render-reflect loop and those that fail despite broad 3D-reasoning gains.
entries.frozen_endpoint_headroom_requirement: To remain paperable beyond a benchmark observation, the candidate needs a prospective pre-outcome feature or controlled intervention that predicts the below-50% basin and separates executable cross-stage binding from long-context, generic underspecification, and spatial-grounding baselines.
entries.frozen_exact_prediction: After matching prompt length, number of constraints, referential ambiguity, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand, Complex Description/Scene Restatement queries will still show lower Pass@1 and a higher concentration of cross-stage intent-to-layout/render binding failures than other VWE-Bench query types; clarifying text alone will not close the gap unless it also resolves executable binding.
entries.frozen_same_information_baseline: A matched long-context plus spatial-grounding baseline that uses query length, constraint count, ambiguity, asset count, distance/angle/object-count demands, and stage-specific grounding/editing errors to predict Pass@1.
entries.frozen_falsifier_expression: Using released VWE-Bench/VibeWorlding-Gym units, construct a matched comparison: sample Complex Description/Scene Restatement failures and easier-query controls matched on length, constraint count, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand; annotate stage-specific errors; optionally generate clarified-query versions. The falsifier is passed if query type no longer predicts Pass@1 or stage-specific binding failure after these controls.

design.reproduction_target: Generate a first-party corpus of 3D scene construction queries spanning Complex Description, Scene Restatement, and control query types (Simple Description, Direct Command), with matched distributions on prompt length, constraint count, referential ambiguity, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand. Execute each query through a first-party end-to-end 3D construction pipeline (LLM-based intent parsing, layout generation, tool-based rendering, reflection) and record Pass@1 and stage-specific failure modes.
design.independent_truth: Ground truth is binary Pass@1 determined by whether the constructed 3D scene satisfies the query constraints as verified by automated geometric/semantic checks (e.g., object count, spatial relations, asset usage) plus human spot-checking. Stage-specific failure labels (intent parsing, layout, rendering, binding) are assigned by blinded annotators examining pipeline traces, with adjudication for disagreements. Query type is assigned at generation time and verified by independent raters. No outcome information is used in query generation or matching.
design.causal_unit: One first-party generated query with linked metadata (query type, covariates), pipeline execution trace, Pass@1 outcome, and stage-error annotation.
design.observable: For each query: query type (Complex/Restatement vs control), matched covariates (length, constraints, ambiguity, assets, rubric difficulty, spatial demand), Pass@1 (binary), and dominant failure stage (intent-to-layout/render binding vs other grounding/editing error).
design.intervention: No method intervention. Construct a matched observational contrast: sample Complex/Restatement queries and control queries matched on all covariates, execute both through the identical pipeline, and compare Pass@1 and binding-failure concentration. Optionally, generate clarified versions of Complex/Restatement queries (resolving ambiguity without changing executable binding requirements) as a secondary contrast to test whether clarification alone closes the gap.
design.same_information_lock: Both the candidate contrast and the baseline predictive model see only: query type, prompt length, constraint count, referential ambiguity score, asset count, rubric difficulty score, spatial-quantity demand score, stage-error labels, and Pass@1. No hidden pipeline internals, no outcome-derived features, no extra model calls beyond the single pipeline execution per query.
design.matched_baseline_execution: Fit the strongest same-information baseline (e.g., logistic regression or gradient-boosted trees) using only length, constraint count, ambiguity, asset count, rubric difficulty, spatial-quantity demand, and stage-specific grounding/editing error indicators to predict Pass@1 and binding-failure concentration. Train and evaluate on the same matched units with the same evaluation budget (same train/test split, same cross-validation folds).
anti_bake_in_controls: Generate queries using templates and randomization that do not condition on the predicted outcome; freeze the query manifest and covariate measurements before any pipeline execution.
Pre-register the matching algorithm (e.g., propensity score matching or exact matching on binned covariates), exclusion rules, and stage-error coding rubric before inspecting any outcomes.
Use blinded independent annotation of stage-specific failures from pipeline traces, with a held-out adjudication subset (20% of cases) to measure inter-rater reliability.
Run a negative-control permutation test: shuffle query-type labels within matched strata and re-run the analysis to confirm the pipeline does not manufacture a spurious query-type effect.

decision_criteria.baseline_reduction_supported: After matching, query type adds no predictive power for Pass@1 or binding-failure concentration beyond the strongest same-information baseline (e.g., likelihood ratio test p>0.05, or change in AUC <0.02), within the frozen matched sample.
decision_criteria.candidate_residual_survives: Complex Description/Scene Restatement queries retain a significant excess of lower Pass@1 (e.g., odds ratio <0.7, p<0.05) or higher cross-stage binding-failure concentration (e.g., odds ratio >1.5, p<0.05) after the strongest same-information baseline and all matching controls.
decision_criteria.inconclusive: First-party query generation fails the equivalence probe (covariate non-overlap, low inter-rater agreement on query type, or trivial/impossible baseline success rate), matched cells are too sparse (<20 units per cell), or stage-error labels are too unreliable (Cohen's kappa <0.6) to separate the candidate from the baseline.

design.single_variable_repair_if_inconclusive: If matched cells are too sparse, increase the number of generated queries per cell (up to the unit cap) while maintaining covariate overlap; if stage-error labels are unreliable, simplify the failure taxonomy to a binary binding-vs-other classification and re-annotate.

scientific_object_invariants: Query type taxonomy: Complex Description and Scene Restatement versus other query types (e.g., Simple Description, Direct Command) preserved as a categorical variable
Matching covariates: prompt length, constraint count, referential ambiguity, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand measured identically across all units
Outcome measure: Pass@1 (binary success/failure) on executable 3D scene construction
Failure mode taxonomy: stage-specific errors including cross-stage intent-to-layout/render binding failures versus other grounding/editing errors
Contrast structure: Complex/Restatement queries show lower Pass@1 and higher binding-failure concentration than matched controls after covariate adjustment
source_specific_dependencies_removed: VWE-Bench released corpus (6,828 queries, 254 evaluation cases)
VibeWorlding-Gym specific query templates and asset libraries
operationalization_recompile.why_dependencies_are_not_scientific_obje: The VWE-Bench corpus is a particular sampling of the broader population of 3D world construction queries; the scientific claim is about the relationship between query type, covariates, and failure modes, not about these specific 254 cases. The query templates and asset libraries are implementation details of one particular benchmark instantiation. Author outcome tables and labels are provenance artifacts; the same measurements (Pass@1, stage errors) can be obtained by running a first-party evaluation pipeline on newly generated queries and annotating failures independently. The scientific object is the conditional association structure, not the specific dataset.
operationalization_recompile.transport_scope: The recompiled experiment tests the same conditional association (query type predicting Pass@1 and binding failures after matching) using first-party generated queries and evaluation. If the residual survives, it supports the claim that this is a general phenomenon in end-to-end 3D construction systems, not specific to VWE-Bench. If the baseline reduction is supported, it falsifies the claim in this first-party context, which is evidence against generality but does not directly falsify the original VWE-Bench observation without further transport argument.
operationalization_recompile.equivalence_probe: Before running the main falsifier, verify that the first-party query generation process produces Complex Description/Scene Restatement queries and control queries that: (1) span overlapping ranges on all matching covariates (length, constraints, ambiguity, assets, rubric difficulty, spatial demand), confirmed by distributional overlap tests (e.g., propensity score overlap, Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests); (2) are rated by blinded human annotators as belonging to the intended query type categories with >80% inter-rater agreement; (3) when submitted to the same 3D construction pipeline, produce a non-trivial baseline success rate (20-80% Pass@1) to ensure the task is neither trivial nor impossible. If any of these checks fail, the first-party operationalization is not faithful to the original scientific object.

evidence_review.reason: The design replaces the frozen VWE-Bench/VibeWorlding-Gym scientific object with a first-party generated query corpus, which prior_support explicitly identified as unavailable (HOLD_SUPPORT_UNAVAILABLE) and required source-specific units with content hashes for independent matching. The operationalization_recompile removes the VWE-Bench corpus, templates, asset libraries, and author outcome tables as 'provenance artifacts,' but the frozen scientific object is defined by the measurable failure-regime boundary within that specific benchmark's query distribution and evaluation pipeline. Generating new queries from parameterized templates bakes in the candidate's own operationalization of 'Complex Description' and 'Scene Restatement' categories, and the equivalence probe cannot independently verify that first-party queries sample the same population as the frozen VWE-Bench units because the source corpus is unavailable. The independent truth (Pass@1 via automated geometric checks on first-party generated scenes) is not the same frozen truth (VWE-Bench per-case Pass@1 from the released evaluation pipeline). The design therefore cannot obtain independent evidence without defining the result into the test.

entries.title: Stateful-feedback validity horizon for self-evolving skill controllers
entries.frozen_irreducible_object: A feedback-validity horizon object for self-evolving agents: given the same initial controller/update schedule and observable early-feedback state, predict whether later persistent-state changes will make the schedule invalid because newly exposed multi-turn defects lie outside the initial error basis. The object must separate feedback-source exhaustion from ordinary nonstationarity, stale supervision, and governance/action-surface changes.
entries.frozen_endpoint_headroom_requirement: The residual must appear on prospective later-round defects before observing endpoint TSR, not by post hoc selection of trajectories where multi-turn feedback wins. It must survive matched feedback quantity, recency, task difficulty, governance action, and harness-state statistics.
entries.frozen_exact_prediction: Under matched model, task distribution, initial feedback, update budget, and harness-state statistics, an update schedule selected from initial single-turn feedback will fail or stagnate when later multi-turn interactions reveal defects outside the initial feedback basis; a stateful feedback-refresh controller will improve on those same units. A generic stale-supervision/nonstationarity baseline given the same feedback recency and occupancy statistics will not predict the basis-mismatch split.
entries.frozen_same_information_baseline: A stale-supervision/nonstationary online-learning baseline that receives the same early and later feedback samples, recency, sample size, occupancy/domain-shift statistics, and update budget, and predicts performance solely from distribution shift and fresh-information availability.
entries.frozen_falsifier_expression: Using the released or reproducible SkillEvo substrate, create matched units with the same initial single-turn feedback and early TSR trajectory. In one arm, keep later defects within the initially revealed gap classes; in the other, introduce later multi-turn defects outside that class while matching task difficulty, model, revision budget, governance, and feedback quantity. Compare an initial-feedback-selected schedule against a stateful feedback-refresh schedule and a generic stale-supervision/nonstationarity baseline. If the generic baseline predicts the split equally well, reject the new problem formulation.

design.reproduction_target: A first-party sandbox environment with synthetic multi-turn tasks, preregistered defect taxonomies, and executable validators that instantiate the feedback-validity horizon object without dependence on SkillEvo assets.
design.independent_truth: Each synthetic multi-turn task is generated with a ground-truth defect specification stored before any schedule arm runs. Defects are labeled within-basis if they belong to gap classes revealed in initial single-turn feedback, outside-basis otherwise. Task success is determined by executing the agent's output against held-out test cases with deterministic validators.
design.causal_unit: A single synthetic multi-turn task instance with fixed initial single-turn feedback, fixed later defect-class assignment (within or outside basis), and a revision/update schedule to be applied.
design.observable: For each unit: initial feedback content and gap-class set, early performance trajectory, later multi-turn defect outcomes, feedback recency, occupancy statistics, update count, and final held-out TSR/defect resolution.
design.intervention: Assign the revision/update schedule: initial-feedback-selected static schedule versus stateful feedback-refresh schedule. The stale-supervision baseline observes identical feedback and predicts from shift/freshness features alone.
design.same_information_lock: All arms receive identical initial feedback, later feedback samples, recency, occupancy statistics, sample sizes, model snapshot, decoding settings, task difficulty strata, and update budget. Only the schedule-selection rule differs.
design.matched_baseline_execution: The stale-supervision/nonstationary baseline is executed on the same units with identical feedback transcripts, recency, occupancy statistics, and update budget. It produces predictions solely from generic shift/freshness features, scored on the same held-out outcomes.
anti_bake_in_controls: Preregister the defect taxonomy, unit-matching variables, schedule rules, baseline features, and decision thresholds before generating any task instances or inspecting outcomes.

Freeze the initial feedback basis, task difficulty stratum, model snapshot, and update budget before assigning schedule arms; any unit failing independent defect verification is excluded as NO_EVIDENCE.
Audit the full accepted revision-action surface so every accepted update produces an independently verifiable persisted artifact change or is rejected before the scientific unit starts.
Use held-out multi-turn evaluation cases disjoint from all feedback and revision-selection cases, with execution order randomized and identical call/token/compute caps across arms.
The synthetic task generator must not encode the predicted threshold/sign/order; defect classes are assigned randomly within strata and verified independently.

decision_criteria.baseline_reduction_supported: The generic stale-supervision baseline, using only matched recency/occupancy/shift features, predicts the within-basis versus outside-basis performance split at least as accurately as the stateful refresh contrast (preregistered equivalence margin), so no basis-mismatch-specific residual remains.
decision_criteria.candidate_residual_survives: On outside-basis units the stateful feedback-refresh schedule improves held-out TSR/defect resolution over the initial-feedback-selected schedule by the preregistered margin while within-basis units do not, and the same-information stale-supervision baseline fails to predict this split.
decision_criteria.inconclusive: The sandbox cannot instantiate the causal variables, defect classes cannot be independently verified, matched units cannot be constructed, or arm outcomes are confounded by unequal feedback quantity, difficulty, update budget, or unverifiable persisted updates.

design.single_variable_repair_if_inconclusive: If the sandbox fails the equivalence probe, adjust the synthetic task generator to ensure initial single-turn feedback reveals a proper subset of later multi-turn defect classes, then re-run the probe before the main falsifier.

entries.review_feedback: The design manufactures the frozen scientific object's core causal variable—the initial feedback basis and its relationship to later multi-turn defect classes—by construction in a synthetic sandbox. The equivalence probe requires confirming that 'initial single-turn feedback reveals a proper subset of later multi-turn defect classes,' which means the sandbox generator is explicitly designed to encode the basis-mismatch structure that the frozen prediction claims to discover. This violates independent_truth_valid because the ground-truth defect specification is generated by the candidate's own sandbox rather than an external environment, and violates no_mechanism_bake_in because the synthetic task generator must produce the exact within-basis/outside-basis split that the candidate mechanism predicts. The prior_support HOLD requires SkillEvo round-level units exposing the same initial feedback basis and later defect classes; the recompile removes these as 'acquisition provenance' but the scientific object invariants explicitly include 'Initial feedback basis' and 'Basis-mismatch condition' as categorical distinctions that cannot be independently established without the source-specific unit structure. The operationalization_recompile claims the 9 production Skills and 98 reference files are not the scientific object, but the frozen object requires separating feedback-source exhaustion from ordinary nonstationarity in a way that depends on the actual relationship between initial feedback and later defects—a relationship that cannot be manufactured without defining the result into the test. The equivalence_probe cannot independently fail because it checks for the very structure the generator was designed to produce.

scientific_object_invariants: Initial feedback basis: the set of gap classes revealed by single-turn feedback at unit initialization
Later defect realization: multi-turn interaction outcomes that fall within or outside the initial basis
Schedule-selection rule: the algorithm mapping feedback state to revision timing (static vs. stateful refresh)
Performance metric: TSR (task success rate) or equivalent defect-resolution rate measured on held-out multi-turn cases
Basis-mismatch condition: the categorical distinction between defects predictable from initial feedback vs. novel defect classes
Information parity: all arms receive identical feedback recency, occupancy statistics, sample sizes, and update budgets
source_specific_dependencies_removed: SkillEvo production Skills corpus (9 specific skills)
SkillEvo proprietary execution environment and logging infrastructure
operationalization_recompile.why_dependencies_are_not_scientific_obje: The 9 production Skills and 98 reference files are specific artifacts that happened to be available to the original authors; they constitute acquisition provenance rather than necessary conditions for the feedback-validity horizon phenomenon. The scientific object requires only that there exist multi-turn tasks with preregisterable defect taxonomies, not that they be the specific SkillEvo tasks. Similarly, the original controller implementations are realizations of schedule-selection rules, not the rules themselves. A first-party sandbox with synthetic multi-turn tasks preserves the causal structure while removing dependence on unavailable author assets.
operationalization_recompile.transport_scope: The recompiled experiment tests the feedback-validity horizon object in a controlled first-party environment with synthetic multi-turn tasks. Results transport to any self-evolving agent setting where: (1) initial feedback is single-turn, (2) later interactions are multi-turn, (3) defect taxonomies can be preregistered, and (4) schedule-selection rules can be manipulated. The specific effect sizes may not transport directly to production-scale systems, but the qualitative basis-mismatch phenomenon and its distinguishability from generic staleness should generalize.
operationalization_recompile.equivalence_probe: Before running the main falsifier, verify that the first-party sandbox instantiates the same causal variables: (1) Generate a small pilot set of multi-turn tasks with preregistered defect taxonomies; (2) Confirm that initial single-turn feedback reveals a proper subset of later multi-turn defect classes; (3) Verify that the stale-supervision baseline, when given only recency/occupancy statistics, cannot distinguish within-basis from outside-basis units in the pilot; (4) Confirm that the stateful refresh controller can be implemented with identical information access to the static schedule. If any check fails, the sandbox does not instantiate the same scientific object.
